The wind howled like a banshee, rattling the panes of the lantern room. Elias, the keeper of the St. Jude Light, watched the grey Atlantic churn below. It was a lonely life, but the solitude suited him.

The next morning, the storm had passed, leaving the beach littered with driftwood and kelp. Elias walked the shoreline, his boots crunching on wet sand. Half-buried in the foam was a green glass bottle, corked tight with wax.

He pried it open. Inside was a single sheet of paper, brittle and yellowed. The handwriting was elegant, dated 1892.
